new_tasks.title: Adversarial description lint follow-ups: non-ASCII coverage, CSV robustness, perf string allocation, trybuild anchor
new_tasks.north_star: T-022's coverage gaps (non-ASCII positive-list test, CSV-no-escape for comma in values, trybuild docs.rs anchor existence, per-desc String allocation in doc claim) are closed.
new_tasks.rationale: The 4-lens code review found several T-022 follow-ups that are individually small but collectively worth tracking as a single task. None is a security regression (T-022 already fires on all non-ASCII via the byte-check added in M-0.9.1 C-3), but the absence of test coverage and doc/perf consistency weakens the maintainability of the defense.
acceptance_criteria: Add a positive-list test in `desc_safety_test.rs` that exercises `contains_only_ascii_printable` with tab (0x09), newline (0x0A), carriage return (0x0D), and a mixed ASCII-only string (0x20-0x7E) — all must pass cleanly. Already covers non-ASCII rejection via C-3 test fixture.

Add whitespace-around-comma coverage for `split_blocklist` in `tokitai-macros/src/description/safety.rs`: `"a, b, c"` should parse to `["a", "b", "c"]` (trimmed). Current implementation does not trim; add a test + fix the parsing.

Add a CSV-escape mechanism for `desc_blocklist`: a comma-containing literal like `"ignore previous, and then"` must be expressible. Minimum: support double-quote wrapping in the env-var CSV parser, or document the limitation and add a trybuild fixture that demonstrates the workaround (use per-tool `desc_blocklist` for comma values).

Verify that the `docs.rs errors.html#E0032` anchor referenced in `tests/ui/desc_safety_injection.stderr` exists on the published tokitai-macros crate. If it does not exist, either create the anchor or change the reference to a valid docs.rs URL.
Update `docs/AI_INTEGRATION.md` table row for T-022 per-call cost from "Zero" to "O(len(desc)) at macro time (allocates for blocklist merge)" to match the implementation.

new_tasks.title: Capability manifest ergonomics: better diagnostics, empty-Vec alloc fix, W023 first-class opt-out
new_tasks.north_star: The capability manifest system has no silent failure modes: every missing declaration triggers a visible diagnostic, every denied capability names the allowlist, and the generated code allocates no Vec for empty slices.
new_tasks.rationale: The code review found 8 ergonomic gaps in T-023's implementation. Most are diagnostic-quality improvements (span at the offending entry rather than the method ident, Display impl missing the allowlist, W023 message missing cross-reference to other `allow` uses). One is a perf regression (Vec allocation for empty CAPABILITIES slice). One is a correctness gap: the `#[tool(requires_invalid)]` flag is silently dropped before the const is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: `CapabilityNotInAllowlist::Display` (in `tokitai-mcp-server/src/server.rs`) names the configured allowlist in the error message, so an operator triaging the failure doesn't need to cross-reference config.

The `#[tool(requires = [...])]` parse-error diagnostic anchors at the offending entry's span, not at the method's ident span. (Currently at method ident; change to the individual entry span in the `requires` list.)

`W023` warning message (in `tokitai-macros/src/tool/mod.rs`) includes a cross-reference to other `allow = [...]` uses (like `allow_short_desc`, `allow_insecure_desc`) so the user knows the suppression pattern is consistent.

`generate_capabilities_consts` in `definitions.rs` skips Vec allocation when `tools` slice is empty (the `CAPABILITIES` const still resolves as `&[]` via a zero-capacity vec or a static reference, not an allocated empty Vec).
`CAN_INVALID` / `requires_invalid` flagged entries are NOT silently dropped before CAPABILITIES const emission — either emit them with an error or document the limitation.
Add a `parse_blocklist_env` visibility reduction: `pub fn` → `pub(crate) fn` (it is only used inside the macros crate and expanding visibility beyond the crate is an accidental API leak).

new_tasks.title: TypedDispatcher and serve() hardening: tools_list caching, env-args integration test
new_tasks.north_star: TypedDispatcher::tools_list is memoized (cached) so repeated calls don't re-validate every spec. The serve() entry point's argument parsing is exercised with real std::env::args in an integration test.
new_tasks.rationale: Two deferred findings from code review: (1) TypedDispatcher::tools_list re-scans every spec on every call — since the spec set is immutable after construction, the result can be cached in the OnceLock. (2) parse_serve_args is unit-tested with a fake argv but never with real std::env::args from an integration test, leaving the boundary where env::args() returns unexpected values unexercised.
acceptance_criteria: TypedDispatcher::tools_list — when called multiple times with the same spec set — returns the cached result after the first call. Cache is a `OnceLock<Vec<...>>` or similar. Test: call tools_list twice and assert pointer equality (same allocation) OR assert time (second call is ~instant).

Add an integration test in `tokitai-mcp-server/tests/version_assertion_test.rs` that calls `serve()` (or its argument-parsing equivalent) with real `std::env::args()` by exercising the binary entry point. If a pure test is impossible, add a doc example or a smoke-test shell script in `examples/`.
Both changes pass CI with no new top-level deps.

new_tasks.title: Code quality / API surface cleaning pass: duplicate docs, undocumented alias, lazy env-var probe
new_tasks.north_star: The public API surface has no duplicate doc comments, no undocumented function aliases, and the env-var probes in the hot macro path are lazy.
new_tasks.rationale: Six low-severity findings from code review that don't belong to any feature-specific task but are worth fixing for consistency: (1) duplicate doc comments on CapabilityManifestProvider trait and capability_in_allowlist; (2) undocumented `run_version_check` alias for `serve`; (3) `category` parsed and stored in a local variable with no error code for silent fall-through; (4) `TOKITAI_PROFILE` / `TOKITAI_QUIET` probed at every macro invocation (not lazy); (5) assert_compatible_with panic messages still do not name the drifted versions (partially addressed by H-1 doc claim fix but implementation remains); (6) T-022 env-var forwarding has no validation that value is non-pathological.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate doc comments on `capability_in_allowlist` (tokitai-core/src/lib.rs ~line 2807) are deduplicated: keep the richer one, remove the orphaned line or merge into the parent item.

`run_version_check` alias for `serve` (tokitai-mcp-server/src/lib.rs:~line 129) is either documented with a `///` doc-comment noting its relationship to `serve()`, or removed in favor of a single entry point.
`category` parsing in `tokitai-macros/src/tool/attrs/method.rs` ~line 665: add an error code for the fall-through case (category set but unused) or remove the variable.

`should_show_warnings()` and `profiling_enabled()` calls in tok-macros/src/tool/mod.rs are hoisted out of the per-method loop into the per-impl-block scope (they only need to be probed once per impl block, not once per method).

`assert_compatible_with` panic messages name both the expected and actual version (currently hardcoded drift-category strings). This may require accepting `const_format_args!` is not stable; use `concat!` in a non-const runtime helper called from the const-eval path.

`TOKITAI_DESC_BLOCKLIST` env-var value forwarded by `tokitai-macros/build.rs` is validated as UTF-8 and non-empty (currently forwarded verbatim without validation; a binary payload in the env var crashes the macro).

new_tasks.title: Critical tokitai-llm bug fixes: Box::leak, double-optional ProviderArgs, anthropic concatenation, Ollama system discard
new_tasks.north_star: tokitai-llm has no silent-correctness bugs. Every subcommand handles its arguments consistently, and every provider preserves message fidelity.
new_tasks.rationale: Four bugs found in the M-0.12.0 code review. (1) `verify/mod.rs:115` uses `Box::leak` to convert LLM-returned String to `&'static str` — leaks one allocation per finding; fix: change `Finding::code` to `String`. (2) `cli/mod.rs:175` wraps `ExamplesArgs.provider` in `Option<ProviderArgs>` when `VerifyArgs` uses a flat `ProviderArgs` — the double-optionality means passing `--provider openai --model gpt-4o` does NOT trigger the LLM pass in `examples::run` (silent degradation to v0.1 stub). (3) `provider/anthropic.rs:146` concatenates multi-block text replies with no separator — `["Hello", " world"]` becomes `"Helloworld"` with no space. (4) `provider/ollama.rs:65` silently discards the system prompt — should at minimum `warn!` the user.
acceptance_criteria: `verify/mod.rs:Finding::code` is `String` (not `&'static str`). No `Box::leak` in the crate.
`ExamplesArgs.provider` is `ProviderArgs` (not `Option<ProviderArgs>`). All four subcommands use the same type for their provider args (flat `ProviderArgs`).
`llm_examples` in `examples/mod.rs` triggers LLM pass when `--provider openai --model gpt-4o` is passed (regression test added).
`provider/anthropic.rs` inserts a space between concatenated `Text` blocks (or joins with newline). Test case: `["Hello", " world"]` → `"Hello world"`.
`provider/ollama.rs:complete_with_tools` logs `warn!` when `system` is `Some` but the provider discards it.
All four provider URLs are precomputed in `new()` instead of reformatted per-request (`format!("{base}/v1/...")` on every call).
All existing tests pass. No regression in any other crate.

new_tasks.title: LLM prompt/code deduplication: extract shared crate::llm module in tokitai-llm
new_tasks.north_star: The three LLM modules (verify, infer-capabilities, examples) share a common `crate::llm` abstraction for building prompts, formatting tool summaries, stripping markdown fences, and pretty-printing schemas. No code is duplicated across modules.
new_tasks.rationale: Code review found four code patterns repeated identically across `verify/mod.rs`, `examples/mod.rs`, and `infer_capabilities/mod.rs`: (a) markdown code-fence stripping (3 copies, 6 lines each), (b) LLM system prompts (3 copies, ~15 lines each with identical "Do not add markdown fences" footer), (c) tool-summary formatter (3 copies, `format!("Tool: ...\nDescription: ...\nSchema: ...")`), (d) schema-pretty-print helper (3 copies, `match t.input_schema_value() { Ok(v) => serde_json::to_string_pretty(&v)..., Err(_) => t.input_schema.clone() }`).
acceptance_criteria: New `tokitai-llm/src/llm/mod.rs` module (or `src/llm.rs`) with `pub fn strip_markdown_fences(s: &str) -> &str`, `pub fn format_tool_summary(t: &ToolDefinition) -> String`, and `pub fn schema_pretty(t: &ToolDefinition) -> String`.
All four patterns above are removed from `verify/mod.rs`, `examples/mod.rs`, and `infer_capabilities/mod.rs` and replaced with calls to `crate::llm::*`.
The system prompt for each subcommand is a dedicated `pub const` exported from `llm/mod.rs` (e.g. `VERIFY_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `EXAMPLES_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `INFER_CAPABILITIES_SYSTEM_PROMPT`).
No semantic changes — the prompts are byte-for-byte identical after the move.
All existing tests pass unchanged.

new_tasks.title: tokitai-llm provider safety hardening: max_tokens, unwrap cleanup, poisoned mutex, dead code
new_tasks.north_star: All providers handle errors gracefully, have no panic paths, and have no dead code. Configuration surfaces (max_tokens, timeouts) are exposed through the CLI.
new_tasks.rationale: Code review found several safety issues. (1) `anthropic.rs:83` hardcodes `max_tokens: 1024` — should be configurable via CLI or a default const. (2) `cache/mod.rs:124` uses `.expect("CacheKey is always serialisable")` — should use `?` or `expect` with proper context. (3) `cache/mod.rs:154,164` uses `lock().ok()?` silently swallowing poisoned-mutex errors — should log or use `lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| ...)`. (4) `openai.rs:181` uses `unwrap_or(Value::Null)` on malformed tool-call arguments — should warn. (5) `infer/mod.rs:173-181` `dispatch_as_tool_message` is dead code (never called from `run`). (6) `infer/mod.rs:102` `build_provider` is `pub` but should be `pub(crate)` — internal helper leaked to public API. (7) Four sites use `unwrap_or("default")` on a value guaranteed `Some` by `build_provider`'s own validation. (8) `infer_capabilities/mod.rs:64` documents JSON Lines output but produces pretty-printed JSON. (9) `ollama.rs:116` clones tool envelopes per request — should precompute. (10) `openai.rs`, `anthropic.rs`, `ollama.rs` all reformat URLs per-request instead of precomputing in `new()`.
acceptance_criteria: `anthropic.rs` `max_tokens` is configurable via CLI (`--max-tokens`) with a reasonable default (1024 documented, 4096 as default).
`cache/mod.rs:124` `.expect` is removed — error handled gracefully (logged at `warn!`, cache miss treated as no-cache).
`cache/mod.rs:154,164` poisoned mutex is logged at `warn!` level before recovering.
`openai.rs:181` malformed tool-call arguments log a `warn!` message before returning `Value::Null`.
`infer/mod.rs:173-181` dead `dispatch_as_tool_message` removed or feature-gated with `#[cfg(feature = "dispatch")]`.
`infer/mod.rs:build_provider` is `pub(crate)` — other modules access it via `crate::infer::build_provider` (already works).
Four `unwrap_or("default")` calls are replaced with direct field access (no default needed after validation).
`infer_capabilities/mod.rs:64` output is JSON Lines (one JSON object per line), not pretty-printed.
`ollama.rs:116` precomputes tool envelopes at provider construction time.
All three providers precompute request URL in `new()` instead of `format!` per request.
All existing tests pass.

new_tasks.title: tokitai-llm test coverage: zero-test modules, LLM-response parsing, cache round-trips
new_tasks.north_star: Every module in tokitai-llm has unit test coverage for its non-HTTP-I/O paths. The critical LLM-response parsing path is exercised with realistic fixture data. Zero-test modules (infer/mod.rs, provider/ollama.rs) have at least basic coverage.
new_tasks.rationale: Code review found 13 tests total, with critical gaps: `infer/mod.rs` has zero tests (including `complete_with_cache`, the most important function in the crate); `ollama.rs` has zero tests; `anthropic.rs` has 1 test; the LLM-response JSON parsing path in all three modules is untested (the existing "parsing" tests only test `serde_json::from_str::<Value>`); cache round-trip for `tool_calls` and `usage` is untested. Adding test coverage with realistic fixture data will prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: `infer/mod.rs`: unit tests for `build_provider` branch coverage (3 provider types), `complete_with_cache` hit/miss/error paths (using a mock or manually constructing the cache), `AnyProvider` dispatch.
`provider/ollama.rs`: unit tests for all 3 `ChatMessage` renderings (User, Assistant with tool_calls, Tool), `OllamaResponse::into_completion` with text response, tool-call response, empty response.
`provider/anthropic.rs`: unit tests for multi-block text accumulation (regression test for separator bug), `ToolUse` mapping, `Other` block ignored.

`verify/mod.rs`: realistic LLM response fixture tests (markdown-fenced JSON, no-fence JSON, malformed JSON, empty findings, multiple findings). `escape_json_pointer` round-trip test. `walk` recursion test with deeply-nested schema.
`examples/mod.rs`: `baked_examples` shape assertion (`[{"input": {...}}]`), `name_contains` filter test, `apply_examples` with multiple tools and partial matches.
`cache/mod.rs`: `CachedResponse <-> CompletionResponse` round-trip with `tool_calls` and `usage` populated. Cache-key sensitivity to `system` prompt, `tools` slice, and message order.
Total test count ≥ 35 (current 13 + 22 new). All existing tests pass.

new_tasks.title: Build integration: TOKITAI_LLM env forwarding in build.rs, full pipeline end-to-end test
new_tasks.north_star: The `TOKITAI_LLM_VERIFY_REPORT` env var flows from operator → build.rs → `option_env!` in the macro without manual steps. An end-to-end shell script exercises the full pipeline: write a `#[tool]` impl → run `tokitai-llm verify --report-path` → set env var → rebuild → verify cargo:warning= lines appear.
new_tasks.rationale: Code review found the LLM pipeline has no automatic integration. `build.rs` does not forward `TOKITAI_LLM_VERIFY_REPORT` (even though the `DEFAULT_VERIFY_REPORT_NAME` constant exists for this purpose). The `#[tool(llm_cache_key = true)]` attribute documented in the llm module is not wired through (always passes `false`). There is no end-to-end test or example that exercises the full pipeline from `#[tool]` → verify report → macro consumes report.
acceptance_criteria: `tokitai-macros/build.rs` forwards `TOKITAI_LLM_VERIFY_REPORT` to the macro (via `cargo:rustc-env=TOKITAI_LLM_VERIFY_REPORT=...` pattern or direct `option_env!` — at minimum document the existing `option_env!` path in `CLAUDE.md`).
`tokitai-macros/build.rs` references `DEFAULT_VERIFY_REPORT_NAME` from `tokitai-macros/src/tool/llm/mod.rs` (remove `#[allow(dead_code)]`).

New end-to-end script or `cargo test` integration test in `tokitai-macros/tests/` that: writes a tmp `#[tool]` source, compiles it, runs `tokitai-llm verify` against the generated binary (or schema), writes the report, sets `TOKITAI_LLM_VERIFY_REPORT`, rebuilds, and asserts `cargo:warning=` appeared.
Wire `#[tool(llm_cache_key = true)]` attribute through `_attrs` in `generate_for_impl` so it actually triggers the cache-key const emission (remove the hardcoded `false`).
`infer` subcommand gains `--schema <json>` arg so the tool-calling loop can actually be exercised from CLI (currently always `Vec::new()`).
All existing tests pass.

new_tasks.title: Provider trait redesign: InferenceRequest struct + tool_choice + response_format + temperature/stop/seed
new_tasks.north_star: The Provider trait uses a structured InferenceRequest (not flat params) with tool_choice, response_format, temperature, stop, seed, parallel_tool_calls, and stream fields. Adding new fields is non-breaking.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: current complete_with_tools(system, messages, tools) is too rigid. Cannot force tool calls via API (tool_choice missing). Cannot control temperature, seed, stop sequences. The flat-param design means every new field is a breaking change.
acceptance_criteria: New `InferenceRequest` struct in `tokitai-llm/src/provider/mod.rs` with: system, messages, tools, tool_choice (Auto/Required/None/Specific(string)), response_format (JsonObject/JsonSchema(Value)), max_tokens, temperature, stop, seed, parallel_tool_calls, stream.
Provider::complete_with_tools signature changes from `(&self, system, messages, tools)` to `(&self, req: &InferenceRequest)`.
All three providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama) use the new fields where applicable, silently ignore where unsupported.
Ollama provider ignores response_format and tool_choice (not supported by Ollama API).
Cache key includes tool_choice, response_format, temperature, seed — changes when these differ.
CLI adds `--tool-choice`, `--response-format`, `--temperature`, `--seed` args.
All 62 existing tests pass unchanged (updated to new signature).

new_tasks.title: Streaming support: BoxStream + closure wrapper for all 3 providers
new_tasks.north_star: Every provider can stream token deltas and tool-call events in real time, with time-to-first-token under 1s.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: each LLM turn takes 5-15s. Streaming cuts time-to-first-token from ~10s to ~1s. Enables pipeline: stream-tool-call → dispatch → stream-result in parallel.
acceptance_criteria: Provider trait gains `async fn complete_streaming(&self, req: &InferenceRequest) -> Result<BoxStream<Result<CompletionEvent>>>` (core BoxStream API).
Convenience `stream_with_callback<F, Fut>(&self, req, cb)` fires closure per event.
CompletionEvent enum: TextDelta(String), ToolCallBegin { index, name }, ToolCallArgsDelta { index, args }, Done(CompletionResponse).
OpenAI: SSE chunk parsing, text_delta + tool_calls delta accumulation.
Anthropic: SSE text_delta + tool_use_begin/delta/end events.
Ollama: /api/chat streaming mode.
When stream: false, complete_streaming falls back to single-shot buffered call.
All existing tests pass unchanged.

new_tasks.title: T-022 safety lint per-category exemption: desc_safety_scope + allow_imperative_desc
new_tasks.north_star: Mathematical tool descriptions, which are inherently imperative, can be exempted from the INSTRUCTION bit while keeping ROLE_HEADER, FAKE_PROMPT, and NON_ASCII_DESC enforcement.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: `#[tool(desc = "Use this to solve polynomial equations. You must provide 'var'.")]` triggers T-022 INSTRUCTION error. Only option is blanket `allow_insecure_desc` which disables all safety checks.
acceptance_criteria: New `desc_safety_scope = "relaxed"` attribute at impl and method level — exempts INSTRUCTION bit only (not ROLE_HEADER, FAKE_PROMPT, NON_ASCII_DESC, OVERSIZED, USER_EXTENSION).
New `#[tool(allow_imperative_desc)]` ident flag — shorthand for `desc_safety_scope = "relaxed"` on INSTRUCTION bit.
Existing `allow_insecure_desc` continues to bypass all T-022 checks.
Works at both impl-level and method-level (mirroring allow_insecure_desc).
No new env-var or per-build flag.
Positive test: allow_imperative_desc + "you must" desc compiles. Negative test: ROLE_HEADER still fires under relaxed.

new_tasks.title: Usage hint auto-injection: ToolDefinition.usage_hint + ToolHintPlacement
new_tasks.north_star: Tools can carry a usage_hint (example call syntax) that is automatically injected into the system prompt by the provider — no manual Jinja hacks.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: models ignore tools[].function.description but read system prompt. Current mathdatiao uses Jinja to inject examples manually. Native support benefits every tokitai user.
acceptance_criteria: ToolDefinition gains `usage_hint: Option<String>` field + `with_usage_hint(self, hint) -> Self` builder.
`#[tool(usage_hint = "sympy_solve(equation='x^2-4', var='x')")]` stores the hint on the generated ToolDefinition.
New ToolHintPlacement enum (AppendToSystem, AsSeparateMessage, None) on ProviderConfig.
When tool_hint_placement != None, provider automatically injects hints into system prompt or as separate message.
Default ToolHintPlacement::None — zero behavioral change.
All existing tests pass unchanged.

new_tasks.title: Tool call result caching: ToolCache with TTL and CacheBackend
new_tasks.north_star: Self-consistency and retry-heavy agent loops avoid redundant tool dispatches via an in-memory result cache.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: self-consistency (5 samples) calls same sympy_solve(eq='x^2-4', var='x') 5 times — 4/5 are wasted MCP calls.
acceptance_criteria: New `ToolCache` struct wrapping `CacheBackend` trait with configurable TTL.
Cache key = (tool_name, serialized arguments JSON). Different args → different cache entry.
Wired into the tool-calling loop: check cache before ToolProvider::call_tool, write after.
Default TTL: 60s (configurable via --tool-cache-ttl).
In-memory by default (reuses InMemoryCache from existing cache/mod.rs).
Self-consistency test: 5 identical calls → 1 real dispatch + 4 cache hits.
All existing tests pass unchanged.

new_tasks.title: Parallel tool execution: ExecutionStrategy enum for concurrent tool dispatch
new_tasks.north_star: When the model returns multiple independent tool calls, they execute concurrently — reducing wall-clock time by 2-3x.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: model calls sympy_factor and sympy_integrate simultaneously. Current tokitai executes them sequentially.
acceptance_criteria: New ExecutionStrategy enum: Sequential, Parallel { max_concurrency }, Pipelined { waves: Vec<Vec<String>> }.
Under Parallel, independent tool calls run via tokio::join_all / futures::future::join_all.
Under Pipelined, wave N waits for wave N-1 but runs concurrently within the wave.
ToolProvider::call_tool is &self (not &mut self) — no locking needed for concurrent dispatch.
ToolCache (T-047) and parallel dispatch compose: cache checks are concurrent too.
CLI adds --execution-strategy and --max-concurrency args.
Default Sequential — zero behavioral change for existing callers.

new_tasks.title: response_format support: JsonObject and JsonSchema for structured output
new_tasks.north_star: Providers support OpenAI-style response_format for structured JSON output.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: needs model to return { "answer": "...", "confidence": 0.95, "tools_used": [...] } as structured JSON, not free text.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAI: ResponseFormat::JsonSchema(schema) → response_format: { type: "json_schema", json_schema: schema }.
OpenAI: ResponseFormat::JsonObject → response_format: { type: "json_object" }.
Anthropic: JsonObject sets anthropic_beta: ["output-json-2025-01-10"] header.
Ollama: silently ignores response_format (not supported).
CLI: --response-format json-schema:<inline-json> or --response-format json-object.
No change to existing behavior when response_format: None.

new_tasks.title: Provider-level middleware hooks: pre_request, post_request, on_error
new_tasks.north_star: Providers support composable middleware for auth-token refresh, OTel logging, and rate limiting.
new_tasks.rationale: Downstream math-agent user: needs retry on 401 (token refresh), outgoing request logging to OTel, and rate limiting for high-concurrency math agents.
acceptance_criteria: New ProviderMiddleware trait: pre_request(&self, req: &mut InferenceRequest), post_request(&self, req, resp, duration), on_error(&self, error, attempt) -> RetryDecision.
RetryDecision enum: Retry { delay }, GiveUp.
Middleware is composable via Vec<Box<dyn ProviderMiddleware>> on ProviderConfig.
Wired into complete_with_tools and complete_streaming (post-request fires after stream ends).
Example middleware: auth-token refresh on 401.
Default empty middleware list = zero behavioral change.
